::: {#fig-positive-negative-parts}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: positive-negative-parts-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Three bar charts side by side, each with the die rolls 1 to 6 on the
#|   horizontal axis. The left chart, f, has bars of height minus 2, minus 1,
#|   0, 1, 2 and 3, the first two below the axis. The middle chart, the
#|   positive part, has bars of height 0, 0, 0, 1, 2 and 3, which sum to 6.
#|   The right chart, the negative part, has bars of height 2, 1, 0, 0, 0
#|   and 0, which sum to 3.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 7
pnp_rolls_pf <- 1:6
pnp_f_pf <- pnp_rolls_pf - 3
pnp_plus_pf <- pmax(pnp_f_pf, 0)
pnp_minus_pf <- pmax(-pnp_f_pf, 0)
pnp_f_tbl_pf <- tibble::tibble(
  x = pnp_rolls_pf, value = pnp_f_pf, panel = "f (sum = 3)"
)
pnp_plus_tbl_pf <- tibble::tibble(
  x = pnp_rolls_pf, value = pnp_plus_pf, panel = "f+ (sum = 6)"
)
pnp_minus_tbl_pf <- tibble::tibble(
  x = pnp_rolls_pf, value = pnp_minus_pf, panel = "f- (sum = 3)"
)
pnp_bars_pf <- dplyr::bind_rows(pnp_f_tbl_pf, pnp_plus_tbl_pf, pnp_minus_tbl_pf)
pnp_aes_pf <- ggplot2::aes(x, value, fill = panel)
pnp_colours_pf <- c("#0072B2", "#009E73", "#D55E00")
ggplot2::ggplot(pnp_bars_pf, pnp_aes_pf) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(panel)) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = pnp_colours_pf) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = pnp_rolls_pf) +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = "none") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Die roll x", y = "Value")
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: positive-negative-parts-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Three bar charts side by side, each with the die rolls 1 to 6 on the
#|   horizontal axis. The left chart, f, has bars of height minus 2, minus 1,
#|   0, 1, 2 and 3, the first two below the axis. The middle chart, the
#|   positive part, has bars of height 0, 0, 0, 1, 2 and 3, which sum to 6.
#|   The right chart, the negative part, has bars of height 2, 1, 0, 0, 0
#|   and 0, which sum to 3.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 7
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

pnp_rolls_pf = np.arange(1, 7)
pnp_f_pf = pnp_rolls_pf - 3
pnp_panels_pf = [
    ("f (sum = 3)", pnp_f_pf, "#0072B2"),
    ("f+ (sum = 6)", np.maximum(pnp_f_pf, 0), "#009E73"),
    ("f- (sum = 3)", np.maximum(-pnp_f_pf, 0), "#D55E00"),
]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(7, 3.5), sharey=True,
                         layout="constrained")
for ax, (title, values, colour) in zip(axes, pnp_panels_pf):
    ax.bar(pnp_rolls_pf, values, color=colour)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xlabel("Die roll x")
axes[0].set_ylabel("Value")
plt.show()
```

:::

Let $D$ be the die rolls of @exm-integral.
The plot shows the [function](functions.qmd#def-function) $f(x) = x - 3$ on $D$,
its [positive part](algebra.qmd#def-positive-negative-parts),
and its [negative part](algebra.qmd#def-negative-part).
With the [counting measure](#def-counting-measure),
each [integral](#def-integral) is the [sum](algebra.qmd#def-summation) of the bar heights,
and $6 - 3 = 3$ is the integral of $f$.

:::
